Sit
SIT
v. (rendering Hebrew yāshab and Greek kathēmai, kathizō)
From Old English sittan, common Germanic, from the Indo-European root *sed- — the same root behind Latin sedere and the English words seat, session, see (a bishop's), and settle. The Hebrew yāshab means both to sit and to dwell or remain, and that double sense governs much of its biblical use: to sit somewhere is to take up residence there, which is why sitting in the seat of the scornful is a matter of settled company rather than a passing posture.

Biblical Definition

Sitting in Scripture signifies settled position, completed work, and authority to judge. Its highest use is Christological. “The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool” (Psa 110:1) is the Old Testament verse most quoted in the New, and the session of Christ — His sitting down at the right hand of the Majesty on high — is the great proof that the sacrificial work is finished, since the Levitical priests stood daily ministering and offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins, but this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down. A seated priest is a finished atonement. Union with Christ then extends the posture to His people: God “hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (Eph 2:6), a present standing rather than a future hope, and the promise to the overcomer is the same, “To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne” (Rev 3:21). Sitting is also the posture of the learner at a teacher's feet — Mary “sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word” (Luk 10:39), and was told she had chosen the good part, which shall not be taken away from her. And it can mark the settled company of the wicked, the third and worst stage of the first psalm's descent: walking in the counsel of the ungodly, standing in the way of sinners, and finally sitting in the seat of the scornful.

Webster 1828 Definition

To rest on the lower part of the body, and in Scripture to be settled, enthroned, or at rest from finished work; the posture of Christ's session at the right hand, of the believer seated in heavenly places in Him, of the disciple at the Master's feet, and of settled company good or evil.

expand to see more

SIT, v.i. 1. To rest upon the buttocks, as animals; to be seated.

2. To rest; to remain; to abide; in which sense the Hebrew word is rendered both to sit and to dwell.

3. To be placed in the seat of authority; to be in a state of rest or of judgment. Sit thou at my right hand. Psalm 110. When the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory. Matt. 25.

4. To be in the posture of a learner. Mary sat at Jesus' feet and heard his word. Luke 10. Paul was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel. Acts 22.

5. To sit down; to begin a siege, or to settle in a place. To sit in the seat of the scornful; to take one's settled place among mockers. Psalm 1.

Key Scripture

Psalm 110:1 — "A Psalm of David. The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool."

Ephesians 2:6 — "And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus:"

Luke 10:39 — "And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word."

Revelation 3:21 — "To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne."

Modern Corruption

The session of Christ is the most neglected article of the creed in ordinary preaching, so that the finished, reigning, interceding Lord is replaced by a Saviour still pleading and a church still trying to secure what He has already obtained.

expand to see more

Christ's sitting down is doctrine, not scenery, and Hebrews argues from the posture itself. Every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices which can never take away sins; but this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God. The standing priest signifies unfinished work; the seated priest signifies a work that cannot be added to. Where the session is neglected, two errors move in. Rome's mass re-presents an offering that Scripture says was made once; and much popular evangelicalism, though it denies any repeated sacrifice, preaches an anxious Christ whose success depends on the response He is given, which quietly undoes the same finality.

The corresponding loss on the believer's side is Eph 2:6. The apostle says God hath made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ — a completed action describing a present position — and this is the foundation for everything he commands in the second half of the letter, including the standing of Eph 6. To treat the Christian's seat in Christ as a future reward that present performance might yet forfeit is to reverse the order of the epistle and to put the believer back on his own footing. The right response is neither presumption nor anxiety but the one the same apostle draws: if ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yāshab means to sit, dwell, or remain, and is used of God who sitteth in the heavens and of Israel dwelling in the land. Greek distinguishes kathizō, to take a seat, from kathēmai, to be seated; sugkathizō is to be seated together, used in Eph 2:6.

expand to see more

Hebrew yāshab (H3427) — to sit, remain, dwell, inhabit; over 1,000 occurrences, covering both posture and settled residence.

Hebrew k'sē' (H3678) — a seat, a throne; the word behind the throne of grace and the throne of judgment.

Greek kathēmai (G2521) — to be seated, to dwell; used of Him that sitteth on the throne throughout Revelation.

Greek kathizō (G2523) — to cause to sit, to sit down; used in Heb 10:12 of the one offering after which He sat down, and in Heb 1:3 of the session on high.

Greek sugkathizō (G4776) — to seat together with; used in Eph 2:6 of believers made to sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus.

Usage

"Of the session and reign of Christ: sit thou at my right hand (Psa 110:1); he sat down on the right hand of God (Heb 10:12)."

"Of the believer's position and prospect: made us sit together in heavenly places (Eph 2:6); to sit with me in my throne (Rev 3:21)."

"Of the disciple and of settled company: Mary sat at Jesus' feet (Luk 10:39); nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful (Psa 1:1)."
